warnings_strict_justification: Ruff selects E, F, I, UP and B only, and the AppInspect gate fails on failures and errors but only reports warnings. https://github.com/bunkerity/bunkerweb-splunk-addon/blob/main/.github/workflows/tests.yml https://github.com/bunkerity/bunkerweb-splunk-addon/blob/main/pyproject.toml
know_secure_design_justification: Théophile Diot (@TheophileDiot), the maintainer, also maintains the BunkerWeb web application firewall and knows secure design principles. The add-on applies them: it ships only configuration files, with no scripts, modular inputs or stored credentials, and its metadata limits writes to the admin and sc_admin roles. Extractions run at search time only, and an event that does not match the whole documented format gets no denial or ModSecurity fields. https://github.com/bunkerity/bunkerweb-splunk-addon/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md https://github.com/bunkerity/bunkerweb-splunk-addon/blob/main/TA-bunkerweb/default/props.conf https://github.com/bunkerity/bunkerweb-splunk-addon/blob/main/TA-bunkerweb/metadata/default.meta
know_common_errors_justification: Théophile Diot (@TheophileDiot), the maintainer of the BunkerWeb web application firewall, knows the common vulnerability classes for this kind of software. For a log parser the main one is request data an attacker controls becoming a trusted field. We anchor each extraction to the whole line, set `KV_MODE = none` on the access and error sourcetypes, and keep adversarial samples (forged reasons, ModSecurity ids and denial lines in user agents, URIs, referrers and hosts) that the live test asserts never become metadata. https://github.com/bunkerity/bunkerweb-splunk-addon/blob/main/TA-bunkerweb/default/props.conf https://github.com/bunkerity/bunkerweb-splunk-addon/blob/main/samples/access_adversarial.log https://github.com/bunkerity/bunkerweb-splunk-addon/blob/main/tests/test_ta.py
